title: Operating System II
description: Operating system concepts: memory management from early schemes to virtual memory, concurrent processing and synchronization, deadlock, device and file management, performance and security. Built from the Ibadan Distance Learning course book for CSC 421 (Ogunseye and Woods).

topics.title: Overview of the Operating System
topics.summary: An operating system is the program that acts as an interface between the user and the hardware, managing memory, processors, devices and files. Systems differ by type (batch, time-sharing, distributed, network, real-time) and all provide services such as program execution, I/O, communication, error handling and protection.
subtopics: Definition and the four managers: memory, processor, device, file
Other activities: security, performance control, job accounting, error aids
Batch, time-sharing, distributed, network and real-time systems
Multitasking and multiprogramming
Operating system services
Protection and resource management

topics.title: Memory Management: Early Systems
topics.summary: Early memory managers loaded each job whole and contiguously: single contiguous allocation, then fixed partitions, dynamic partitions with first-fit or best-fit placement, and relocatable dynamic partitions with compaction. Each scheme trades simplicity against fragmentation.
subtopics: Placement, replacement and fetch strategies
Single contiguous allocation
Fixed partitions and internal fragmentation
Dynamic partitions: first fit, best fit, next fit, worst fit
Relocatable dynamic partitions and compaction
Bounds and relocation registers

topics.title: Virtual Memory
topics.summary: Virtual memory lets a job run without being wholly in main memory. Paged and demand-paged allocation divide jobs into equal pages tracked by job, page map and memory map tables, page replacement policies such as FIFO and LRU decide what to swap out, and segmentation divides jobs into logical modules.
subtopics: Virtual memory: advantages and disadvantages
Paged memory allocation: JT, PMT and MMT
Demand paging, swapping and the page interrupt handler
Locality of reference and working sets
Page replacement: FIFO, LRU and others
Segmented and segmented/demand-paged memory

topics.title: Concurrent Processing and Process Synchronization
topics.summary: Multiprocessing systems run processes on several processors, arranged as master/slave, loosely coupled or symmetric configurations. Processes sharing a resource must synchronize so only one is in a critical region at a time, using test-and-set, WAIT and SIGNAL, or semaphores, as in the producers-and-consumers and readers-and-writers problems.
subtopics: Multiprogramming, multiprocessing and parallel processing
Master/slave, loosely coupled and symmetric configurations
Critical regions and mutual exclusion
Test-and-set, WAIT and SIGNAL
Semaphores: P and V
Producers and consumers, readers and writers; concurrent programming

topics.title: Deadlock, Starvation and Race Conditions
topics.summary: Deadlock is a system-wide tangle in which jobs hold resources while waiting for resources held by others. It needs four conditions at once (mutual exclusion, resource holding, no preemption, circular wait), and the operating system can prevent, avoid (Banker's algorithm), detect (directed graphs) or recover from it.
subtopics: Deadlock and the four necessary conditions
Seven cases of deadlock
Modelling deadlock with directed graphs
Prevention and Havender's ordering
Avoidance: safe states and the Banker's algorithm
Detection, recovery, starvation and race conditions

topics.title: Device and File Management
topics.summary: The device manager allocates dedicated, shared and virtual devices and schedules disk requests to keep seek time low (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, LOOK, C-SCAN). The file manager organizes files sequentially, directly or indexed, and stores them contiguously, chained or indexed, with an access control matrix for permissions.
subtopics: Dedicated, shared and virtual devices
Sequential and direct access storage; seek, search and transfer time
I/O subsystem: channels, control units, interrupts, DMA, buffers
Disk scheduling: FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, LOOK, C-SCAN, C-LOOK
File organization and record formats
Contiguous, chained and indexed storage; access control matrix

topics.title: System Performance and Security
topics.summary: Performance is measured by turnaround time, response time, throughput, capacity and resource utilization, evaluated with timing, benchmarks and simulation, and kept stable with feedback loops. Security protects resources through access control, surveillance, auditing and passwords at the physical, human, operating system and network levels.
subtopics: Performance measures: turnaround, response, throughput, capacity, utilization
Evaluation techniques: timing, instruction mixes, benchmarks, simulation
Benchmarks: Whetstone, LINPACK, Dhrystone
Bottlenecks, saturation and feedback loops
Security measures: access control, surveillance, auditing, passwords
Levels of protection: physical, human, operating system, network
